checks.Title: Seduce, don't just observe
checks.Evidence: Long stretches lead with mechanism and procedure — schism physics, weapon nomenclature, cut-by-cut fight choreography, contract/relay logistics — before any sensory or emotional hook lands; texture like 'the camphor,' 'the warm chip,' or the lumen mice appears late, sparsely, and is quickly subordinated to plot/exposition (e.g., the Gingerbread House's uncanny resin colors are noted once and then the scene pivots straight into tactical soldier-assessment).
checks.Fix: Open scenes by dwelling in one or two strange-beautiful sensory details (the wrong-colored resin, the warm damp credstick, the mice's cold light) for several beats before the tactical/expository machinery takes over, so allure precedes and outweighs the procedural horror.

checks.Title: Open with the world doing its work
checks.Evidence: The story opens directly with plot-relevant sensory/technical exposition (Kyle detecting a schism at 17-19 hertz, measuring its width, rerouting) rather than a grounded, mundane entry beat; within the first page we're already into world-jargon and escalating danger with no commute/transaction moment that isn't laden with plot mechanics.
checks.Fix: Precede the schism-detection beat with a brief, lower-stakes routine moment (e.g., him buying coffee, navigating ordinary traffic) that lets the reader settle into the world's textures before the plot machinery (schisms, hertz bands, tracking teams) starts demanding comprehension.

checks.Title: Gloss first mentions in-voice, never dump
checks.Evidence: Terms like 'CorpoNations,' 'GLMZ,' 'neuretics,' 'Splicer,' 'Φ' (currency), 'Praxis,' 'Carrion,' and 'the Ghost Period' are dropped in with zero orientation — e.g. 'the CorpoNation property registry sometime in the 2190s' or 'GLMZ night' assumes the reader already knows what these zones/factions are, and later terms like 'Atlas NeoCortex,' 'the sixty-four,' and 'the aperture' pile up in dense lore-exposition paragraphs that read as pure info-dump rather than in-voice gloss.
checks.Fix: Introduce each proprietary term through a concrete sensory or functional detail the first time Kyle's POV encounters it (as was done reasonably well with 'schism' and 'the array'), and cut or redistribute the late-manuscript exposition blocks (e.g. the Atlas NeoCortex/sixty-four splices explanation) into smaller, scene-grounded beats rather than standalone lecture paragraphs.

checks.Title: Never an acronym before its term
checks.Evidence: GLMZ appears repeatedly ('the GLMZ night', 'any GLMZ block') with no full-term gloss anywhere in the story, and the acronym E.L.F. is used ('The E.L.F. signal, the one Ledger had picked up') without ever spelling out what it stands for.
checks.Fix: Introduce the full term in-voice at first use (e.g., 'the Greater Loop Metro Zone—GLMZ—night' and a comparable gloss for E.L.F.) before allowing the bare acronym to recur.

checks.Title: Give the POV character one human crack
checks.Evidence: The girl-with-the-teeth beat does exactly what the commandment asks: 'What he didn't let himself count was the girl in the hallway, behind the curtain, watching him the way children watch a thing they've already decided to remember,' followed later by him crouching to her height and opening his hand — a soft, unguarded moment that has nothing to do with his function as a fighter, immediately followed by him cleaning the blade and moving on to logistics.

checks.Title: Land one beat past the handoff
checks.Evidence: The manuscript closes with a warm, resolved domestic beat — Kyle eating soup at Pixel's table, 'The city needed nothing from him tonight,' 'He picked up the spoon with the hand that still worked right. He ate.' — which reads as comfort and closure rather than a quiet gesture that adds weight or cost for a cold reader; the actual weighted material (the lie to the last soldier, the entity's revelation, nine dead predecessors) is explicitly set aside and 'carried alone,' undercutting the landing instead of being the landing.
checks.Fix: End instead on the unresolved image of the fifth thing Kyle refuses to put away — the lowered blade, the broken promise, the soldier who trusted it — held in silence at the doorway before he crosses to Pixel's, so the last beat is the cost he's keeping rather than the meal that lets him set it down.

checks.Title: Reward re-reading without requiring it
checks.Evidence: The manuscript plants dense recursive material clearly designed to reward a second pass (the 17-19 Hz motif tying schisms to the entity, Pixel's beacon, the 'ten configurations' revelation, the false offer to the last soldier), but stretches like the AI dialogue exchange ('carousel: the call, unresolved... you collect things too') and the Gingerbread House info-dump require the reader to already hold a large amount of continuity to parse cleanly on a first read, risking first-pass comprehension rather than just deepening it.
checks.Fix: Trim or clarify the elliptical AI-dialogue and threshold-revelation passages so a first-time reader can follow the literal chain of events without needing prior installments, while keeping the coded phrasing intact for returning readers to re-decode.

checks.Title: Elevate, don't reconstruct
checks.Evidence: The excerpt piles unexplained proper nouns and mythology onto a newcomer at an accelerating rate (NeoCortex, Atlas variant, Praxis, Carrion supply lines, the Ghost Period, the Cinderfall, the 127 seconds, 'nine before him,' Marrow, the Gingerbread House, Able, Sift, Renner, Carver) with almost no orientation given in-scene; by the final third the prose assumes the reader already holds a working mental map of the whole cosmology ('He knew which of the sixty-four would call that unforgivable') rather than adding doors into it.
checks.Fix: Add brief grounding beats the first time each major proper noun/faction is invoked (a clause of context, an image, or a sensory anchor) so a first-time reader can track who Praxis, the entity, and the nine predecessors are without already knowing the series, rather than layering new lore-callbacks on top of each other.

checks.Title: Orient through GLMZ's five pillars
checks.Evidence: The prose weaves all five pillars into functional texture: the entity's LOG GAP revelation ('Ten configurations were deployed... The aperture does not survive the arrival') frames AIs as agenda-driven agents with stakes; nanites appear ambiently in Pixel's suturing/array calibration and the mesh under Kyle's skin; neuretics/NeoCortex explicitly divide him from baseline humans ('the ungoverned lattice... sixty-four of them') and are tied to cost/rarity; Schism is rendered physically and mechanically ('a low hum in the 17-to-19 hertz band... a tear in the world') with Advisory zones and tracking teams; and CorpoNations/gray zones appear via 'the CorpoNation property registry,' the Tier boundary surveillance grid, and 'Off the books meant off the watching.'
